summary: The Radiation Exposure Compensation Reauthorization Act of 2026 amends the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act to expand eligibility categories, increase base compensation amounts, add medical benefits, broaden the list of compensable diseases and covered geographic locations, and extend program deadlines.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for increased compensation of $150,000, additional medical expense reimbursements, and expanded geographic and time boundaries.
affected_groups.group: Downwinders and individuals exposed to atmospheric testing

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for increased base compensation of $150,000, expanded ZIP code eligibility, and updated rules for survivor and representative claims.
affected_groups.group: Individuals affected by Manhattan Project waste

affected_groups.effect: Subject to new health studies conducted by the National Institutes of Health and expanded access to screening and education programs.

key_provisions: Extends temporal and geographic criteria for atmospheric testing claims, including adding Guam and specific cleanup and response locations.
Updates and expands ZIP codes for Manhattan Project waste claims across Missouri, Illinois, Washington, Colorado, and Ohio.
Increases compensation amounts for downwinder and Manhattan Project waste claims to $150,000 and adds reimbursement for documented out-of-pocket medical expenses.

Permits the Attorney General to accept sworn affidavits from third parties as supplementary evidence to substantiate employment history, physical presence, testing or cleanup participation, and disease contraction.
Broadens the definition of authorized agents who may file claims on behalf of deceased or incapacitated individuals.
Expands the list of specified compensable cancers and diseases, including adding renal disease, thyroid disease, and several specific primary cancers.
Extends the authorization of the compensation fund to 2043 and the limitation on filing claims to 2042.
missing_information: Total estimated cost of the program expansions and specific budgetary offsets.
Detailed procedural rules the President will establish for considering petitioner cohort class designations.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Radiation Exposure Compensation Reauthorization Act of 2026 amends the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act to expand eligibility categories, increase base compensation amounts, add medical benefits, broaden the list of compensable diseases and covered geographic locations, and extend program deadlines.
summary_detail.significance: The bill significantly alters the federal radiation exposure compensation framework by expanding qualifying locations and medical conditions, raising compensation payouts, and extending the program's operating lifespan through 2043.
